verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah son of Hilkiah. And it happened in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, that I was in the citadel of Susa.
verses.1:2: And Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and men from Judah; and I questioned them about the Jews who had remained and survived from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
verses.1:3: And they said to me, "Those who remained and were left from the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and in reproach; and the wall of Jerusalem is torn down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
verses.1:4: And when I had heard words of this kind, I sat down and wept and mourned for many days; I was fasting and praying before the face of the God of heaven,
verses.1:5: and I said, "I implore You, Lord God of heaven, strong, great, and fearsome, who keep covenant and mercy with those who love You and keep Your commandments:
verses.1:6: let Your ears be listening and Your eyes open, so that You may hear the prayer of Your servant, which I am praying before You today, night and day, for the sons of Israel, Your servants; and I confess for the sins of the sons of Israel, by which they have sinned against You; I and the house of my father have sinned;
verses.1:7: we have been led astray by vanity, and we have not kept Your commandment, and the ceremonies, and the judgments which You prescribed to Moses Your servant.
verses.1:8: Remember the word that You commanded Moses Your servant, saying, 'When you have transgressed, I will scatter you among the peoples;
verses.1:9: and if you return to Me, and keep My precepts, and do them, even if you have been carried away to the farthest parts of heaven, from there I will gather you and bring you back into the place which I have chosen so that My name might dwell there.'
verses.1:10: And they themselves are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great strength and by Your mighty hand.
verses.1:11: I plead with You, Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant, and to the prayer of Your servants who desire to fear Your name; and direct Your servant today, and give him mercy before this man." For I was the cupbearer of the king.
verses.2:1: Now it happened in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that wine was before him, and I lifted up the wine and gave it to the king; and I was as though ailing before his face.
verses.2:2: And the king said to me, "Why is your countenance sad, though I do not see you sick? This is not for nothing; rather, some evil or other is in your heart." And I feared greatly, even exceedingly,
verses.2:3: and I said to the king, "King, live forever! Why should my countenance not grieve, since the city, the house of the tombs of my father, is desolate, and its gates have been burned with fire?"
verses.2:4: And the king said to me, "For what thing are you asking?" And I prayed to the God of heaven,
verses.2:5: and I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant is pleasing before your face, send me into Judea, to the city of the tomb of my father, and I will build it."
verses.2:6: And the king said to me, and the queen who was sitting beside him, "Until what time will your journey be, and when will you return?" And it was pleasing before the countenance of the king, and he sent me; and I appointed a time for him.
verses.2:7: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors of the region beyond the river, so that they may conduct me across until I come into Judea,
verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, so that he may give me timber, that I may be able to cover the gates of the tower of the house, and the walls of the city, and the house that I will enter." And the king gave them to me according to the good hand of my God with me.
verses.2:9: And I came to the governors of the region beyond the river, and I gave them the letters of the king. Now the king had sent with me commanders of soldiers and horsemen.
verses.2:10: And Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard, and they were grieved with great affliction because a man had come who sought the prosperity of the sons of Israel.
verses.2:11: And I came to Jerusalem, and I was there for three days.
verses.2:12: And I rose up by night, I and a few men with me, and I did not tell anyone what God had put in my heart to do in Jerusalem; and there was no beast with me except the animal on which I was riding.
verses.2:13: And I went out through the Valley Gate by night, and before the Fountain of the Dragon, and to the Dung Gate, and I was inspecting the torn-down wall of Jerusalem and its gates consumed by fire.
verses.2:14: And I passed on to the Fountain Gate and to the king's aqueduct, and there was no room for the beast on which I was riding to pass through.
verses.2:15: And I went up along the torrent by night, and I was inspecting the wall; and turning back, I came to the Valley Gate and returned.
verses.2:16: Now the magistrates did not know where I had gone or what I was doing; and indeed, up to that point I had not told anything to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the magistrates, nor to the rest who were doing the work.
verses.2:17: And I said to them, "You know the affliction in which we are, that Jerusalem is desolate and its gates have been consumed by fire; come, and let us build the walls of Jerusalem, and let us no longer be a reproach."
verses.2:18: And I told them of the hand of my God, that it was good with me, and the words of the king which he had spoken to me, and I said, "Let us rise and build." And their hands were strengthened for good.
verses.2:19: Now Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard, and they mocked us and despised us, and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
verses.2:20: And I returned them an answer, and said to them, "The God of heaven Himself helps us, and we are His servants; let us rise and build; for you, however, there is no portion, nor justice, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
verses.3:1: And Eliashib the high priest rose up, and his brothers the priests, and they built the Flock Gate; they consecrated it and set up its doors, and as far as the tower of a hundred cubits they consecrated it, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
verses.3:2: And next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to him Zaccur son of Imri built.
verses.3:3: Now the sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they covered it, and set up its doors, and bolts, and bars. And next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, built.
verses.3:4: And next to him Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, built; and next to them Zadok son of Baana built.
verses.3:5: And next to them the Tekoites built; however, their nobles did not submit their necks in the work of their Lord.
verses.3:6: And Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah built the Old Gate; they covered it, and set up its doors, and bolts, and bars.
verses.3:7: And beside them, Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, men of Gibeon and Mizpah, built for the governor who was in the region beyond the river.
verses.3:8: And next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, built; and next to him Hananiah, the son of a perfumer, built; and they left Jerusalem as far as the wall of the broader street.
verses.3:9: And next to him Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of the district of Jerusalem, built.
verses.3:10: And next to him Jedaiah son of Harumaph built opposite his own house; and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah built.
verses.3:11: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab built half of the district, and the Tower of the Ovens.
verses.3:12: And next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half of the district of Jerusalem, built, he and his daughters.
verses.3:13: And Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah built the Valley Gate; they built it, and set up its doors, and bolts, and bars, and a thousand cubits in the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
verses.3:14: And Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, built the Dung Gate; he built it, and set up its doors, and bolts, and bars.
verses.3:15: And Shallum son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the territory of Mizpah, built the Fountain Gate; he built it, and covered it, and set up its doors, and bolts, and bars, and the walls of the Pool of Siloam toward the king's garden, and as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half of the district of Beth-zur, built as far as opposite the tomb of David, and as far as the pool that was constructed with great labor, and as far as the house of the mighty men.
verses.3:17: After him the Levites built: Rehum son of Bani; after him Hashabiah, ruler of half of the district of Keilah, built in his own district.
verses.3:18: After him their brothers built: Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half of Keilah;
verses.3:19: and next to him Ezer son of Joshua, ruler of Mizpah, built a second measure, opposite the ascent of the strongest corner.
verses.3:20: After him, on the mountain, Baruch son of Zaccai built a second measure, from the corner as far as the gate of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
verses.3:21: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, built a second measure, from the gate of the house of Eliashib as far as the house of Eliashib extended.
verses.3:22: And after him the priests built, men from the plains of the Jordan.
verses.3:23: After him Benjamin and Hasshub built opposite their own house; and after him Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, built opposite his own house.
verses.3:24: After him Binnui son of Henadad built a second measure, from the house of Azariah as far as the bend, and as far as the corner.
verses.3:25: Palal son of Uzai, opposite the bend and the tower that projects from the upper house of the king, that is, in the court of the prison; after him, Pedaiah son of Parosh.
verses.3:26: Now the Nethinim lived in Ophel, as far as opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the tower that jutted out.
verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites built a second measure opposite, from the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the temple.
verses.3:28: Now above the Horse Gate the priests built, each one opposite his own house.
verses.3:29: After them Zadok son of Immer built opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, built.
verses.3:30: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, built a second measure; after him Meshullam son of Berechiah built opposite his own treasury. After him Malchijah, the son of a goldsmith, built as far as the house of the Nethinim and of those selling small wares, opposite the Judicial Gate, and as far as the upper room of the corner.
verses.3:31: And between the upper room of the corner and the Flock Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants built.
verses.4:1: Now it happened, when Sanballat had heard that we were building the wall, that he became very angry; and greatly agitated, he mocked the Jews,
verses.4:2: and he said before his brothers and the throng of the Samaritans, "What are the feeble Jews doing? Will the nations let them alone? Will they sacrifice, and finish in one day? Will they be able to build the stones from the heaps of dust, which have been burned?"
verses.4:3: Moreover, Tobiah the Ammonite, who was next to him, said, "Let them build! If a fox climbs up, it will leap over their stone wall."
verses.4:4: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt; turn back the reproach upon their head, and give them over to contempt in a land of captivity.
verses.4:5: Do not cover their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out before Your face, because they have derided the builders.
verses.4:6: Therefore we built the wall, and we joined the whole of it up to half of it; and the heart of the people was stirred up to work.
verses.4:7: Now it happened, when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the scar of the wall of Jerusalem had closed over and that the breaches had begun to be closed up, that they became exceedingly angry.
verses.4:8: And they all assembled together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to contrive ambushes.
verses.4:9: And we prayed to our God, and we set guards on the wall day and night against them.
verses.4:10: Now Judah said, "The strength of the bearer has weakened, and there is too much earth, and we will not be able to build the wall."
verses.4:11: And our adversaries said, "Let them not know and let them remain unaware until we come into their midst, and kill them, and make the work cease."
verses.4:12: Now it happened, as the Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times from all the places from which they had come to us,
verses.4:13: that I stationed the people in order in the place behind the wall all around, with their swords, spears, and bows.
verses.4:14: And I looked closely and rose up, and I said to the nobles and magistrates, and to the rest of the common people, "Do not be afraid before their face; remember the great and fearsome Lord, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses."
verses.4:15: Now it happened, when our enemies heard that it had been reported to us, that God frustrated their plan. And we all returned to the walls, each one to his own work.
verses.4:16: And it happened from that day that half of their young men did the work, and half were ready for war; and there were spears, shields, bows, and coats of mail, and the leaders were behind them in all the house of Judah.
verses.4:17: Of those building on the wall, and carrying burdens, and loading them, each one did the work with one hand and held a sword with the other.
verses.4:18: For each one of those building was girded at his waist with a sword. And they were building, and they were sounding the horn beside me.
verses.4:19: And I said to the nobles, and to the magistrates, and to the rest of the common people, "The work is great and wide, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another;
verses.4:20: in whatever place you hear the blast of the trumpet, run together to us there; our God will fight for us.
verses.4:21: And let us ourselves do the work, and let half of us hold spears from the rising of the dawn until the stars come out."
verses.4:22: At that time also I said to the people, "Let each one with his servant remain in the midst of Jerusalem, and let us have turns by night and day for working."
verses.4:23: Now I and my brothers, and my servants, and the guards who were behind me, did not take off our clothes; each one undressed only for washing.
verses.5:1: And a great outcry of the people and their wives arose against their brothers, the Jews.
verses.5:2: And there were some who said, "Our sons and our daughters are far too many; let us get grain for their price, and eat, and live."
verses.5:3: And there were some who said, "Let us pledge our fields, our vineyards, and our houses, and let us get grain in the famine."
verses.5:4: And others said, "Let us borrow money for the king's taxes, and let us give our fields and vineyards;
verses.5:5: and now, just as the flesh of our brothers is, so is our flesh, and just as their sons are, so also are our sons. Look, we are subjecting our sons and our daughters to servitude, and some of our daughters are maidservants, and we have nothing with which they can be redeemed, and others possess our fields and our vineyards."
verses.5:6: And I became exceedingly angry when I heard their outcry according to these words.
verses.5:7: And my heart deliberated within me, and I rebuked the nobles and the magistrates, and said to them, "Are each of you exacting interest from your brothers?" And I gathered a great assembly against them,
verses.5:8: and said to them, "We, as you know, have redeemed our brothers, the Jews, who had been sold to the nations, according to our ability; and will you then sell your brothers, and shall we redeem them?" And they were silent, and found nothing to answer.
verses.5:9: And I said to them, "It is not a good thing that you are doing; why have you not walked in the fear of our God, so that we may not be reproached by the nations, our enemies?
verses.5:10: I also, and my brothers, and my servants, have lent money and grain to very many. Let us together not demand this back; let us forgive the debt that is owed to us.
verses.5:11: Restore to them today their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses; moreover, give on their behalf even the hundredth part of the money, grain, wine, and oil that you are accustomed to exact from them."
verses.5:12: And they said, "We will restore them, and we will require nothing from them; and we will do just as you say." And I called the priests and put them under oath to do according to what I had said.
verses.5:13: Furthermore, I shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man who does not fulfill this word from his house and from his labors; so may he be shaken out and become empty." And the entire multitude said, "Amen," and they praised God. Therefore the people did as had been said.
verses.5:14: Now from that day on which the king had commanded me to be governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, for twelve years, I and my brothers did not eat the provisions that were owed to the governors.
verses.5:15: But the former governors, who had been before me, burdened the people and took from them in bread, wine, and money forty shekels every day; moreover, their attendants also oppressed the people. But I did not do so because of the fear of God;
verses.5:16: rather, I built in the work of the wall, and I did not buy a field, and all my servants were gathered for the work.
verses.5:17: The Jews also and the magistrates, one hundred fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations that are around us, were at my table.
verses.5:18: Now there was prepared for me each day one ox and six choice rams, besides birds, and every ten days various wines, and I provided many other things; furthermore, I also did not require the provisions of my governorship, for the people were greatly weakened.
verses.5:19: Remember me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.
verses.6:1: Now it happened, when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall and that no breach remained in it (though up to that time I had not set the doors in the gates),
verses.6:2: that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, and let us make a covenant together in the villages in the plain of Ono." But they themselves were planning to do me harm.
verses.6:3: Therefore I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work, and I cannot come down, so that it may not by chance be neglected when I come and go down to you."
verses.6:4: And they sent to me according to this word four times, and I answered them according to the former statement.
verses.6:5: And Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time according to the former word, and he had a letter in his hand written in this way:
verses.6:6: "It has been heard among the nations, and Geshem has said, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel, and therefore you are building the wall, and you wish to raise yourself up as king over them; for which reason
verses.6:7: you have also appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judea.' The king is going to hear these words; therefore come now, so that we may take counsel together."
verses.6:8: And I sent to them, saying, "It has not happened according to these words that you speak, for out of your own heart you are inventing these things."
verses.6:9: For all of these were trying to frighten us, thinking that our hands would cease from the work and we would rest; for which reason I strengthened my hands all the more.
verses.6:10: And I entered the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, in secret. And he said, "Let us confer together in the house of God, in the midst of the temple, and let us shut the doors of the sanctuary, for they are coming to kill you, and by night they are coming to put you to death."
verses.6:11: And I said, "Does anyone like me flee? And who like me will enter the temple and live? I will not enter."
verses.6:12: And I understood that God had not sent him, but that he had spoken to me as though prophesying, and that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
verses.6:13: For he had received payment so that, being frightened, I would do it and sin, and they would have something evil with which to reproach me.
verses.6:14: Remember me, Lord, on account of Tobiah and Sanballat, according to such deeds of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophet and the rest of the prophets who were trying to frighten me.
verses.6:15: Now the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days.
verses.6:16: Therefore it happened, when all our enemies heard, that all the nations that were around us were afraid, and collapsed within themselves, and knew that this work had been done by God.
verses.6:17: And in those days also, many letters from the nobles of the Jews were being sent to Tobiah, and from Tobiah were coming to them.
verses.6:18: For there were many in Judea who had his oath, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Johanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah;
verses.6:19: moreover, they were also praising him before me, and they were reporting my words to him; and Tobiah was sending letters to frighten me.
verses.7:1: Now after the wall had been built, and I had set the doors in place and enrolled the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites,
verses.7:2: I gave orders to my brother Hanani and to Hananiah, the commander of the house, concerning Jerusalem (for he himself seemed like a truthful man and one fearing God more than the rest),
verses.7:3: and I said to them, "Let the gates of Jerusalem not be opened until the heat of the sun." And while they were still standing by, the gates were shut and barred; and I stationed guards from among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, individually in their turns, and each one opposite his own house.
verses.7:4: Now the city was exceedingly wide and large, and the people were few in the midst of it, and the houses had not been built.
verses.7:5: Now God put it in my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the magistrates, and the common people so that I might enroll them; and I found the book of the census of those who had come up at first, and it was found written in it:
verses.7:6: These are the sons of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away; and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judea, each one to his own city.
verses.7:7: They came with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nahum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.7:8: the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two;
verses.7:9: the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two;
verses.7:10: the sons of Arah, six hundred fifty-two;
verses.7:11: the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Joshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred eighteen;
verses.7:12: the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four;
verses.7:13: the sons of Zattu, eight hundred forty-five;
verses.7:14: the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty;
verses.7:15: the sons of Binnui, six hundred forty-eight;
verses.7:16: the sons of Bebai, six hundred twenty-eight;
verses.7:17: the sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred twenty-two;
verses.7:18: the sons of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-seven;
verses.7:19: the sons of Bigvai, two thousand sixty-seven;
verses.7:20: the sons of Adin, six hundred fifty-five;
verses.7:21: the sons of Ater, the sons of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
verses.7:22: the sons of Hashum, three hundred twenty-eight;
verses.7:23: the sons of Bezai, three hundred twenty-four;
verses.7:24: the sons of Hariph, one hundred twelve;
verses.7:26: the sons of Bethlehem and Netophah, one hundred eighty-eight.
verses.7:27: The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.7:29: The men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three.
verses.7:30: The men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one.
verses.7:31: The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two.
verses.7:32: The men of Bethel and Ai, one hundred twenty-three.
verses.7:33: The men of the other Nebo, fifty-two.
verses.7:34: The men of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.

verses.7:37: The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-one.
verses.7:38: The sons of Senaah, three thousand nine hundred thirty.
verses.7:39: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah in the house of Joshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
verses.7:40: The sons of Immer, one thousand fifty-two.
verses.7:41: The sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
verses.7:42: The sons of Harim, one thousand seventeen. The Levites:
verses.7:43: the sons of Joshua and Kadmiel, of the sons
verses.7:45: the sons of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight.
verses.7:46: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, one hundred thirty-eight.
verses.7:47: The Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.7:48: the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon, the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai,

verses.7:53: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
verses.7:54: the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
verses.7:55: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
verses.7:56: the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha.
verses.7:57: The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
verses.7:58: the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
verses.7:59: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth, who was descended from Zebaim, the son of Amon.
verses.7:60: All the Nethinim and the sons of the servants of Solomon, three hundred ninety-two.
verses.7:61: Now these are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, and they could not show the house of their fathers and their seed, whether they were from Israel:
verses.7:62: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred forty-two.
verses.7:63: And of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.7:64: These searched for their written record in the census and did not find it; and they were expelled from the priesthood.
verses.7:65: And the Tirshatha said to them that they should not eat from the most holy things until a learned and instructed priest should stand up.
verses.7:66: The whole multitude, as one man, was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.7:67: besides their male servants and female servants, who were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven, and among them male singers and female singers, two hundred forty-five.
verses.7:68: Their horses, seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;
verses.7:69: their camels, four hundred thirty-five; donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.7:70: Now some of the leaders of the families gave for the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasury one thousand drachmas of gold, fifty bowls, and five hundred thirty priestly tunics.
verses.7:71: And some of the leaders of the families gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand drachmas of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
verses.7:72: And what the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand drachmas of gold, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priestly tunics.
verses.7:73: Now the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the rest of the common people, the Nethinim, and all Israel lived in their cities.
verses.8:1: And the seventh month had arrived, and the sons of Israel were in their cities. And all the people gathered together as one man to the square that is before the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded Israel.
verses.8:2: Therefore Ezra the priest brought the law before the multitude of men and women, and all who were able to understand, on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And he read in it plainly in the square that was before the Water Gate, from morning until midday, in the sight of the men and women and the wise; and the ears of all the people were alert to the book.
verses.8:4: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a wooden platform, which he had made for speaking; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shemaiah, and Anaiah, and Uriah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, at his right hand, and on the left, Pedaiah, Mishael, and Malchijah, and Hashum, and Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
verses.8:5: And Ezra opened the book before all the people, for indeed he was elevated above the entire people; and when he had opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.8:6: And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God; and all the people answered, "Amen, amen," lifting up their hands; and they bowed down and worshiped God, prostrate to the ground.
verses.8:7: Furthermore, Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, the Levites, were maintaining silence among the people for the hearing of the law; and the people were standing in their station.
verses.8:8: And they read in the book of the law of God distinctly and plainly for understanding; and they understood as it was being read.
verses.8:9: And Nehemiah (that is, the Tirshatha), and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were interpreting, said to the entire people, "The day is consecrated to the Lord our God; do not mourn, and do not weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.
verses.8:10: And he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods, and drink honeyed wine, and send portions to those who have not prepared for themselves, for the day of the Lord is holy; and do not be saddened, for indeed the joy of the Lord is our strength."
verses.8:11: And the Levites were maintaining silence among all the people, saying, "Be silent, for the day is holy, and do not grieve."
verses.8:12: So all the people went away to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great rejoicing, because they had understood the words that he had taught them.
verses.8:13: And on the second day the leaders of the families of the entire people, the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe, so that he might interpret to them the words of the law.
verses.8:14: And they found written in the law that the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses that the sons of Israel should dwell in booths on the festival day, in the seventh month,
verses.8:15: and that they should proclaim and publish word in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, "Go out to the mountain, and bring boughs of olive, and boughs of the most beautiful tree, boughs of myrtle, and branches of palms, and boughs of a thickly leafed tree, so that booths may be made, as it is written."
verses.8:16: And the people went out and brought them. And they made booths for themselves, each one on his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the square of the Water Gate, and in the square of the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.8:17: Therefore the entire assembly of those who had returned from captivity made booths and dwelt in booths; for the sons of Israel had not done so from the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day. And there was exceedingly great rejoicing.
verses.8:18: And he read in the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day until the last day. And they observed the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day a solemn assembly according to the rite.
verses.9:1: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the sons of Israel assembled in fasting and in sackcloth, with earth upon them.
verses.9:2: And the seed of the sons of Israel was separated from every son of a foreigner; and they stood and were confessing their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
verses.9:3: And they rose up to stand, and they read in the scroll of the law of the Lord their God four times in the day, and four times they were confessing and worshiping the Lord their God.
verses.9:4: And Jeshua, and Bani, and Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani rose up upon the platform of the Levites, and they cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
verses.9:5: And the Levites Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bunni, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, Pethahiah said, "Arise, bless the Lord your God from eternity to eternity; and let them bless the name of Your glory, exalted in all blessing and praise.
verses.9:6: You Yourself, Lord, alone, You made heaven, and the heaven of heavens, and all their host; the earth, and all things that are in it; the seas, and everything that is in them; and You give life to all these things, and the host of heaven worships You.
verses.9:7: It is You Yourself, Lord God, who chose Abram, and brought him out from the fire of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham;
verses.9:8: and You found his heart faithful before You, and You struck a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give it to his seed; and You fulfilled Your words, because You are righteous.
verses.9:9: And You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their cry by the Red Sea.
verses.9:10: And You gave signs and wonders upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants, and upon all the people of that land; for You knew that they had acted arrogantly against them; and You made a name for Yourself, even as on this day.
verses.9:11: And You divided the sea before them, and they crossed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; but their pursuers You cast into the deep, like a stone into mighty waters.
verses.9:12: And in a pillar of cloud You were their guide by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, so that the way along which they were going might appear to them.
verses.9:13: You also came down to Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right judgments and a law of truth, ceremonies, and good precepts;
verses.9:14: and You showed them Your consecrated Sabbath; and commandments, and ceremonies, and the law You commanded them by the hand of Moses Your servant.
verses.9:15: You also gave them bread from heaven in their hunger, and You brought out water from the rock for them when they were thirsty, and You told them to enter and possess the land over which You lifted up Your hand to deliver it to them.
verses.9:16: But they and our fathers acted arrogantly, and hardened their necks, and did not listen to Your commandments.
verses.9:17: And they refused to listen, and did not remember Your wonders that You had done for them. And they hardened their necks, and appointed a leader so that they might return to their servitude, as if through contention. But You, a forgiving God, gracious and merciful, long-suffering and of great compassion, did not abandon them,
verses.9:18: even when they had made for themselves a molten calf, and had said, 'This is your god, who brought you out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies;
verses.9:19: yet You, in Your many mercies, did not abandon them in the desert: the pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day to lead them on the way, and the pillar of fire by night to show them the path along which they should go.
verses.9:20: And You gave Your good Spirit to teach them; and Your manna You did not withhold from their mouth, and You gave them water in thirst.
verses.9:21: For forty years You fed them in the desert, and nothing was lacking to them: their garments did not grow old, and their feet were not worn down.
verses.9:22: And You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and You apportioned lots to them; and they possessed the land of Sihon, and the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
verses.9:23: And You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven, and You brought them to the land about which You had spoken to their fathers, that they should enter and possess it.
verses.9:24: And the sons came and possessed the land, and You humbled before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and You gave them into their hand, and their kings, and the peoples of the land, so that they might do to them as pleased them.
verses.9:25: So they captured fortified cities and rich soil, and possessed houses full of all good things: cisterns built by others, vineyards, and olive groves, and many fruit-bearing trees; and they ate, and were filled, and grew fat, and abounded in delights in Your great goodness.
verses.9:26: But they provoked You to wrath, and departed from You, and cast Your law behind their backs; and they killed Your prophets, who were admonishing them to return to You; and they committed great blasphemies.
verses.9:27: And You gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they afflicted them. And in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven, and according to Your many compassions You gave them saviors, who would save them from the hand of their adversaries.
verses.9:28: And when they had rested, they returned to doing evil in Your sight, and You abandoned them in the hand of their enemies, and they possessed them. And they turned back and cried out to You; but You heard from heaven, and You rescued them in Your mercies, many times.
verses.9:29: And You admonished them to return to Your law. But they acted arrogantly, and did not listen to Your commandments, and sinned against Your judgments, which a man will do and live in them; and they gave a withdrawing shoulder, and hardened their neck, and did not listen.
verses.9:30: And You prolonged many years over them, and admonished them in Your Spirit through the hand of Your prophets; and they did not listen, and You delivered them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
verses.9:31: Yet in Your most abundant mercies You did not bring them to complete destruction, nor did You abandon them; for You are a God of compassions, and gracious.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, our God, great, mighty, and awesome, who keeps covenant and mercy, do not turn away from Your face all the hardship that has found us, our kings, and our leaders, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, and all Your people, from the days of the king of Assyria even to this day.
verses.9:33: And You are righteous in all things that have come upon us; for You have acted in truth, while we have acted wickedly.
verses.9:34: Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our fathers did not carry out Your law, and did not heed Your commandments and Your testimonies that You testified among them.
verses.9:35: And they themselves, in their kingdoms, and in Your great goodness that You had given them, and in the very broad and fertile land that You had delivered in their sight, did not serve You, nor did they turn back from their most wicked pursuits.
verses.9:36: Look, we ourselves are slaves today; and as for the land that You gave to our fathers so that they might eat its bread and what is good in it, we ourselves are slaves in it.
verses.9:37: And its crops are multiplied for the kings whom You have set over us because of our sins; and they rule over our bodies and over our livestock according to their will; and we are in great distress."
verses.9:38: Therefore, because of all these things, we ourselves make a covenant and write it down, and our leaders, our Levites, and our priests seal it.
verses.10:1: Now those who sealed it were Nehemiah the Tirshatha, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
verses.10:8: Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah: these were the priests.
verses.10:9: Next, the Levites were Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
verses.10:10: and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
verses.10:14: The heads of the people were Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
verses.10:28: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, and the singers, the Nethinim, and all who separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters,
verses.10:29: all who were able to understand, pledging on behalf of their brothers, their nobles, and those who came to promise and to swear that they would walk in the law of God, which He had given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, that they would do and keep all the commandments of the Lord our God, and His judgments and His ceremonies,
verses.10:30: and that we would not give our daughters to the people of the land, and would not take their daughters for our sons.
verses.10:31: Also, as for the peoples of the land who bring wares and all things for use on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a consecrated day. And we will forgo the seventh year and the exaction of every hand.
verses.10:32: And we will establish ordinances upon ourselves to give a third part of a shekel each year for the work of the house of our God,
verses.10:33: for the loaves of presentation, and for the perpetual sacrifice, and for the perpetual burnt offering on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, on the solemn feasts, and for the consecrated offerings, and for the sin offering so that propitiation may be made for Israel, and for every use of the house of our God.
verses.10:34: Therefore we cast lots concerning the offering of wood among the priests, the Levites, and the people, that it should be brought into the house of our God according to the houses of our fathers, at set times, from the times of one year to the next, to burn on the altar of the Lord our God, just as it is written in the law of Moses,
verses.10:35: and that we would bring the first produce of our land, and the firstfruits of all the fruit of every tree, from year to year, to the house of the Lord,
verses.10:36: and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, just as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our oxen and of our sheep, that they should be offered in the house of our God to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
verses.10:37: And we will bring the firstfruits of our food and of our drink offerings, and the fruit of every tree, also of the vintage and of the oil, to the priests, to the treasury of our God, and the tenth part of our land to the Levites. The Levites themselves will receive the tithes from all the cities of our labors.
verses.10:38: And the priest, the son of Aaron, will be with the Levites in the tithes of the Levites, and the Levites will offer the tenth part of their tithe in the house of our God, to the treasury, into the treasure house.
verses.10:39: For to the treasury the sons of Israel and the sons of Levi will bring the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil; and there will be the consecrated vessels, and the priests, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the ministers; and we will not abandon the house of our God.
verses.11:1: Now the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem, while the rest of the people cast lots to take one part out of ten who were to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine parts in the cities.
verses.11:2: And the people blessed all the men who had offered themselves of their own accord to live in Jerusalem.
verses.11:3: Therefore these are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah. And each one lived in his own possession, in their cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the Nethinim, and the sons of the servants of Solomon.
verses.11:4: And in Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin: of the sons of Judah, Athaiah son of Aziam, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel; of the sons of Perez,
verses.11:5: Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite:
verses.11:6: all these sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight valiant men.
verses.11:7: Now these are the sons of Benjamin: Shallum son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah,
verses.11:8: and after him, Gabbai, Sallai: nine hundred twenty-eight,
verses.11:9: and Joel son of Zichri was their chief officer, and Judah son of Senuah was second over the city.
verses.11:10: And of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,
verses.11:11: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, leader of the house of God,
verses.11:12: and their brothers who did the work of the temple: eight hundred twenty-two. And Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah,
verses.11:13: and his brothers, leaders of the fathers: two hundred forty-two. And Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,
verses.11:14: and their brothers, very mighty men: one hundred twenty-eight, and their chief officer was Zabdiel, son of the mighty men.
verses.11:15: And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni,
verses.11:16: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, over all the works that were outside in the house of God, from among the leaders of the Levites.
verses.11:17: And Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, the leader for praising and for giving thanks in prayer, and Bakbukiah, second among his brothers, and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun:
verses.11:18: all the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four.
verses.11:19: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers who guarded the doors, one hundred seventy-two.
verses.11:20: And the rest of Israel, the priests and the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, each one on his own property.
verses.11:21: And the Nethinim, who lived in Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa of the Nethinim.
verses.11:22: And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica. Of the sons of Asaph were the singers in the ministry of the house of God.
verses.11:23: For an ordinance of the king was over them, and an order among the singers for each day,
verses.11:24: and Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah, son of Judah, was at the king's hand concerning every matter of the people,
verses.11:25: and in the houses throughout all their regions. Some of the sons of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and in its daughters, and in Dibon and in its daughters, and in Kabzeel and in its small villages,
verses.11:26: and in Jeshua, and in Moladah, and in Beth-pelet,
verses.11:27: and in Hazar-shual, and in Beersheba and in its daughters,
verses.11:28: and in Ziklag, and in Meconah, and in its daughters,
verses.11:29: and in Rimmon, and in Zorah, and in Jarmuth,
verses.11:30: Zanoah, Adullam, and in their villages, Lachish and its regions, and Azekah and its daughters. And they remained in Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
verses.11:31: Now the sons of Benjamin, from Geba: Michmash, and Ai, and Bethel and its daughters,
verses.11:35: and Ono, the Valley of Craftsmen.
verses.11:36: And of the Levites were portions of Judah and Benjamin.
verses.12:1: Now these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
verses.12:6: Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah, Shallum, Amok, Hilkiah,
verses.12:7: Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their brothers in the days of Joshua.
verses.12:8: Moreover, the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who were over the hymns, they and their brothers;
verses.12:9: and Bakbukiah and Unni, and their brothers, each one in his own duty.
verses.12:10: Now Joshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib fathered Joiada,
verses.12:11: and Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
verses.12:12: Now in the days of Joiakim, there were priests and leaders of the families: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
verses.12:13: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Johanan;
verses.12:14: of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
verses.12:15: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.12:16: of Adaiah, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
verses.12:17: of Abijah, Zichri; of Mijamin and Moadiah, Piltai;
verses.12:18: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jonathan;
verses.12:19: of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
verses.12:20: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
verses.12:21: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verses.12:22: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as leaders of the families, and the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.12:23: The sons of Levi, the leaders of the families, were recorded in the book of the words of the days, even up to the days of Jonathan the son of Eliashib.
verses.12:24: And the leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Joshua the son of Kadmiel, and their brothers in their turns, to praise and give thanks according to the command of David, the man of God, and to keep watch equally in order.
verses.12:25: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were guards of the gates and of the vestibules before the gates.
verses.12:26: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Joshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
verses.12:27: Now at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought out the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem and celebrate the dedication and rejoicing with thanksgiving and song, and with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
verses.12:28: And the sons of the singers were gathered together from the plains around Jerusalem, and from the villages of the Netophathites,
verses.12:29: and from the house of Gilgal, and from the regions of Geba and Azmaveth; for the singers had built villages for themselves all around Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: And the priests and the Levites were cleansed, and they cleansed the people, the gates, and the wall.
verses.12:31: Then I had the leaders of Judah go up onto the wall, and I stationed two large choirs of those giving praise. And they went to the right on the wall toward the Dung Gate.
verses.12:32: And Hoshaiah went after them, and half of the leaders of Judah,
verses.12:33: and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
verses.12:34: And from the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
verses.12:35: and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the instruments of song of David, the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was before them at the Fountain Gate.
verses.12:36: And opposite them they went up by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall above the house of David, and as far as the Water Gate to the east.
verses.12:37: And the second choir of those giving thanks went on the opposite side, and I after it, and half of the people on the wall, and above the Tower of the Ovens, and as far as the very broad wall,
verses.12:38: and above the Gate of Ephraim, and above the Old Gate, and above the Fish Gate, and the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of Emath, and as far as the Gate of the Flock; and they stood at the Gate of the Guard,
verses.12:39: and the two choirs of those giving praise stood in the house of God, and I, and half of the magistrates with me.
verses.12:40: And the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Mijamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets,
verses.12:41: and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Johanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang out clearly, and Jezrahiah was the overseer;
verses.12:42: and they offered great sacrifices on that day and rejoiced, for God had made them joyful with great joy; and their wives and children also were glad, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.
verses.12:43: They also assigned men on that day over the storerooms of the treasury for the drink offerings, the firstfruits, and the tithes, so that the leaders of the city might bring in the priests and the Levites through them in the beauty of thanksgiving; for Judah was made joyful in the priests and the Levites who stood in attendance.
verses.12:44: And they kept the charge of their God and the charge of expiation, and so did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and of Solomon his son,
verses.12:45: for in the days of David and Asaph from the beginning, there were appointed leaders of the singers praising and giving thanks to God in song.
verses.12:46: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions to the singers and to the gatekeepers day by day, and they consecrated the Levites, and the Levites consecrated the sons of Aaron.
verses.13:1: Now on that day it was read in the scroll of Moses in the hearing of the people, and it was found written in it that an Ammonite and a Moabite must not enter into the assembly of God forever,
verses.13:2: because they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, and they hired Balaam against them to curse them; and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
verses.13:3: Now it happened, when they had heard the law, that they separated every foreigner from Israel.
verses.13:4: And Eliashib the priest was over this, who had been placed in charge of the treasury of the house of our God and was closely related to Tobiah.
verses.13:5: Therefore he made for himself a large treasury, and there before him they had been storing offerings, frankincense, vessels, and the tithe of grain, wine, and oil, the portions of the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the priestly firstfruits.
verses.13:6: Now during all these things I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king, and at the end of some days I asked the king.
verses.13:7: And I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in making for him a treasure room in the forecourts of the house of God.
verses.13:8: And it seemed very evil to me. And I threw the furnishings of the house of Tobiah outside from the treasury;
verses.13:9: and I commanded, and they cleansed the treasuries; and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, the sacrifice, and the frankincense.
verses.13:10: And I learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and that each one of the Levites, and of the singers, and of those who ministered had fled to his own region.
verses.13:11: And I brought a case against the magistrates and said, "Why have we abandoned the house of God?" And I gathered them together and made them stand at their stations.
verses.13:12: And all Judah brought the tithe of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.
verses.13:13: And we appointed over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and next to them Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, because they were proved faithful, and to them were entrusted the portions of their brothers.
verses.13:14: Remember me, my God, for this, and do not blot out my acts of mercy that I have done in the house of my God and in its ceremonies.
verses.13:15: In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, carrying heaps, and loading onto donkeys wine, grapes, figs, and every load, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I gave solemn warning that they should sell on a day on which it was lawful to sell.
verses.13:16: And Tyrians lived in it, bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise, and they were selling on the Sabbaths to the sons of Judah in Jerusalem.
verses.13:17: And I rebuked the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?
verses.13:18: Did not our fathers do these things, and our God bring all this evil upon us and upon this city? Yet you are adding wrath upon Israel by violating the Sabbath."
verses.13:19: Now it happened, when the gates of Jerusalem had grown quiet on the Sabbath day, that I spoke, and they shut the doors, and I commanded that they should not open them until after the Sabbath; and I appointed some of my servants over the gates, so that no one would bring in a load on the Sabbath day.
verses.13:20: And the merchants and those selling every kind of merchandise stayed outside Jerusalem once and twice.
verses.13:21: And I solemnly warned them and said to them, "Why are you staying opposite the wall? If you do this a second time, I will lay a hand on you." Therefore from that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.
verses.13:22: I also told the Levites that they should cleanse themselves and come to guard the gates and to sanctify the Sabbath day. Therefore for this also remember me, my God, and spare me according to the multitude of Your mercies.
verses.13:23: Moreover in those days I saw Jews taking Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite wives.
verses.13:24: And their children spoke half in the language of Ashdod, and they did not know how to speak in the language of Judah, and they spoke according to the language of each people.
verses.13:25: And I rebuked them and cursed them. And I struck some of the men among them and made them bald, and I made them swear by God that they would not give their daughters to their sons, and would not take any of their daughters for their sons or for themselves, saying,
verses.13:26: "Did not Solomon king of Israel sin in a matter of this kind? And surely among many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God set him as king over all Israel; yet foreign women led even him into sin.
verses.13:27: Shall we also, being disobedient, do all this great evil, to transgress against our God and take foreign wives?"
verses.13:28: Now one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, and I drove him away from me.
verses.13:29: Remember, Lord my God, against those who defile the priesthood and the priestly and Levitical ordinance.
verses.13:30: Therefore I cleansed them from all foreigners, and I appointed the orders of the priests and of the Levites, each one in his ministry,
verses.13:31: and in the offering of wood at the appointed times, and in the firstfruits. Remember me, my God, for good. Amen.

notes.1:1: "Hilkiah" translates the Vulgate's Helchiae (matching a Septuagint variant), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Hacaliah.
notes.1:5: The Vulgate renders Hebrew ha-El ("the God") as the adjective fortis ("strong"), producing three attributes: "strong, great, and fearsome."
notes.1:7: "We have been led astray by vanity" follows the Vulgate's vanitate seducti sumus, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "we have acted very corruptly against you." The Vulgate also reads singular "commandment" and "ceremonies" (caeremonias) for Hebrew "statutes."
notes.1:11: "Direct Your servant" translates the Vulgate's dirige servum tuum, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text asks God to "grant success" to His servant.
notes.2:1: "And I was as though ailing before his face" follows the Vulgate's affirmative et eram quasi languidus ante faciem ejus, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a negative ("and I had not been sad in his presence").
notes.2:14: "The king's aqueduct" translates the Vulgate's aquaeductum regis, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the King's Pool."
notes.2:18: "And I said" follows the Vulgate's first-person singular et aio, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads third-person plural ("and they said").
notes.2:20: The Vulgate uses present indicative "helps us" (juvat) and hortatory subjunctive "let us rise and build" (surgamus et aedificemus), where the Hebrew uses future indicatives ("will give us success... we will arise and build").
notes.3:1: Throughout chapter 3, the Vulgate uniformly uses aedifico ("build") where the Hebrew distinguishes between "build" and "repair/strengthen." Here it also reads "Flock Gate" (portam gregis, Hebrew "Sheep Gate") and renders the Hebrew Tower of the Hundred (Meah) as "the tower of a hundred cubits" (turrim centum cubitorum).
notes.3:5: "Of their Lord" translates the Vulgate's singular Domini sui (referring to God), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has plural "their lords" (understood either as their supervisors or as an honorific plural for God).
notes.3:8: "They left Jerusalem as far as the wall of the broader street" translates the Vulgate's dimiserunt ... murum plateae latioris, whereas the Hebrew is often understood as "they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall."
notes.3:15: "Pool of Siloam" translates the Vulgate's piscinae Siloe, identifying the Hebrew Pool of Shelah with the Siloam pool of John 9:7. Other notable Vulgate readings in this section include "half of the district" in 3:11 (Hebrew "a second section"), "the strongest corner" in 3:19 (Hebrew "the armory at the angle"), "on the mountain" in 3:20 (Hebrew "zealously"), "of the Jordan" in 3:22, and "the wall of the temple" in 3:27 (Hebrew "the wall of Ophel").
notes.4:2: In native 4:2-4 (Saints.Bible 3:34-36), the Vulgate preserves several distinctive readings: "Will the nations let them alone?" (Hebrew "Will they restore it for themselves?"), "build the stones" (Hebrew "revive the stones"), "it will leap over" (transiliet in 4:3, Hebrew "break down"), and "to contempt" (in despectionem in 4:4, Hebrew "to plunder").
notes.4:6: Native Vulgate Nehemiah 4:1-6 map to Saints.Bible 3:33-38, and native 4:7-23 map to Saints.Bible 4:1-17. Latin usque ad partem dimidiam literally reads "up to the half part" (half of its extent or height, without specifying altitudo).
notes.4:7: The Vulgate renders the repair of the wall with the vivid medical idiom 'the scar had closed over' (obducta esset cicatrix), reflecting the Hebrew figure of healing.
notes.4:12: The Vulgate construes the difficult final clause (ex omnibus locis quibus venerant ad nos) as identifying where the Jews had come from rather than quoting direct speech, and in v. 7 reads in ordinem ('in order') where the Hebrew has 'by families.'
notes.4:16: The Vulgate reads juvenum eorum ('of their young men') rather than the Hebrew 'my young men' or 'my servants.'
notes.4:18: Stage 1 verified typo fix: adopted Clem1598-USFX reads correct 'ædificantium' (fixing 'ædificentium' in prior editions); native Vulgate 4:18 maps to Saints.Bible 4:12.
notes.4:21: With the hortatory subjunctives faciamus ('let us do') and teneat ('let ... hold') and the pronoun nostrum ('of us'), the Vulgate continues Nehemiah's speech through v. 15 rather than shifting to past-tense narrative as in the Hebrew; similarly, v. 12 has plural verbs (aedificabant, et clangebant) rather than a singular trumpeter.
notes.4:23: The Vulgate renders an obscure Hebrew clause mentioning water as unusquisque tantum nudabatur ad baptismum ('each one undressed only for washing,' lit. 'for baptism/bathing').
notes.5:2: The Vulgate adds pro pretio eorum ('for their price'), making explicit the exchange of children for grain.
notes.5:8: The Vulgate adds ut scitis ('as you know') and reads et redimemus eos ('and shall we redeem them?') where the Hebrew has 'so that they may be sold to us.'
notes.5:10: Aes alienum is the standard Latin idiom for 'debt' (lit. 'another's money'), and the Vulgate reads 'forgive the debt that is owed to us' rather than the Hebrew reference to leaving off interest.
notes.5:15: The Vulgate adds quotidie ('every day') and groups bread, wine, and money into forty shekels daily, whereas the Hebrew mentions bread and wine 'besides forty shekels of silver' without 'daily.'
notes.6:2: The Vulgate translates percutiamus foedus ('let us make a covenant') where the Hebrew reads 'let us meet together,' and renders in viculis ('in the villages') as a common noun rather than a proper place name.
notes.6:9: The Vulgate renders the final clause as first-person narrative (confortavi manus meas, 'I strengthened my hands') rather than an imperative prayer ('Strengthen my hands!') as in the Hebrew.
notes.6:10: The Vulgate reads secreto ('in secret') where the Hebrew describes Shemaiah as 'shut in' or 'confined.'
notes.6:14: The Vulgate adds mei ('Remember me') with Domine ('Lord,' rather than 'my God') and uses the masculine noun in Noadiae prophetae ('Noadiah the prophet') rather than the Hebrew 'prophetess.'
notes.6:16: The Vulgate reads conciderent intra semetipsos ('collapsed within themselves') rather than the Hebrew 'fell greatly in their own eyes,' and a Deo ('by God') without 'our.'
notes.7:1: The Vulgate uses the active first-person verb recensui ("I had enrolled"), portraying Nehemiah as taking a roll of the temple personnel, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a passive ("were appointed").
notes.7:2: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "commander of the citadel over Jerusalem" literally as principi domus de Jerusalem ("the commander of the house, concerning Jerusalem," though de Jerusalem can also be read with domus as "of Jerusalem"), and adds videbatur ("seemed") alongside quasi ("like").
notes.7:3: Unlike the Hebrew, which continues Nehemiah's direct commands throughout the verse, the Vulgate ends the speech after "until the heat of the sun" and shifts to narrative past ("the gates were shut and barred; and I stationed").
notes.7:21: Latin filii Hezeciae (corresponding to Hebrew "of Hezekiah") is grammatically ambiguous and can be construed either as nominative plural ("the sons of Hezekiah") or as genitive singular in apposition to Ater ("son of Hezekiah").
notes.7:47: Latin Nathinaei ("the Nethinim") transliterates the Hebrew title for the hereditary guild of temple servants.
notes.7:48: Native Clementine Vulgate 7:48 combines Saints.Bible 7:47 and 7:48.
notes.7:59: The Vulgate construes Hebrew "the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Amon" as a single lineage ("the sons of Pochereth, who was descended from Zebaim, the son of Amon") rather than two separate clans.
notes.7:65: Latin Athersatha ("the Tirshatha") transliterates the Persian title for the governor, and the Vulgate distinctively renders Hebrew "for Urim and Thummim" as doctus et eruditus ("learned and instructed").
notes.7:70: Here and in verses 71-72, the Vulgate renders the Hebrew currency and weight terms as drachmas (drachmas) and minas (mnas).
notes.8:4: The Vulgate reads singular 'quem fecerat ad loquendum' ("which he had made for speaking") rather than the Hebrew plural "which they had made for the purpose," and renders the second name as 'Semeia' (Shemaiah; Hebrew: Shema).
notes.8:7: The Vulgate reads 'silentium faciebant in populo ad audiendam legem' ("were maintaining silence among the people for the hearing of the law"), whereas the Hebrew has the Levites explaining the law to the people.
notes.8:9: Latin 'Athersatha' ("the Tirshatha") transliterates the Persian official title 'ha-tirshatha' ("the governor").
notes.8:10: The Vulgate translates sweet drink specifically as 'mulsum' ("honeyed wine") and reads first-person plural 'fortitudo nostra' ("our strength"), where the Hebrew has second-person plural ("your strength").
notes.8:15: The Vulgate reads 'ligni pulcherrimi' ("the most beautiful tree") where the Hebrew specifies the wild olive ("oil tree").
notes.9:3: The Vulgate reads 'quater in die, et quater' ("four times in the day, and four times"), whereas the Hebrew specifies a fourth part of the day for reading and another fourth part for confession and worship.
notes.9:7: The Vulgate translates 'Ur of the Chaldeans' etymologically as 'de igne Chaldæorum' ("from the fire of the Chaldeans"), reflecting an ancient interpretive tradition linking the place-name Ur to the Hebrew word for fire.
notes.9:17: 'Dederunt caput' (literally "they gave a head") renders the idiom for appointing a leader, and 'quasi per contentionem' ("as if through contention") represents the Vulgate's rendering of the Hebrew "in their rebellion."
notes.9:32: The Vulgate reads 'ne avertas a facie tua' ("do not turn away from Your face"; Hebrew: "let it not seem little before You") and singular 'regis Assur' ("the king of Assyria"; Hebrew plural: "the kings of Assyria").
notes.9:36: The Vulgate reads 'panem ejus' ("its bread") where the Hebrew has "its fruit."
notes.9:38: As in the Hebrew, chapter 10 begins with this verse. Latin foedus renders Hebrew amanah ('binding agreement') with the standard covenant term. Native Vulgate Nehemiah 9:38 maps to Saints.Bible 10:1 (10:1-39 to 10:2-40), and native 12:33 covers Saints 12:33-34 (shifting native 12:34-46 to Saints 12:35-47).
notes.10:1: Latin Athersatha ("the Tirshatha") transliterates the Persian title hattirshata ('the governor'), borne by Nehemiah (cf. Neh 8:9).
notes.10:27: The Vulgate reads Haran here, whereas the Hebrew text reads Harim (cf. Harem in v. 6).
notes.10:29: The Vulgate renders this clause distinctively as 'pledging on behalf of their brothers' (spondentes pro fratribus suis) and 'to promise and to swear' (ad pollicendum et jurandum), where the Hebrew reads 'joining with their brothers' and 'entering into a curse and an oath.'
notes.10:39: The Vulgate lists four distinct groups in the order 'priests, singers, gatekeepers, and ministers' (et ministri), separating the Hebrew participle ha-mesharetim ('who minister') from the priests.
notes.11:4: The Vulgate reads Aziam here, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Uzziah; the Clementine punctuation also joins 'of the sons of Perez' to the following verse rather than exclusively to Athaiah.
notes.11:7: The Vulgate reads Sellum (Shallum), where the Hebrew text reads Sallu.
notes.11:14: Latin filius potentium ('son of the mighty men') translates Hebrew ben-haggedolim as a descriptive title rather than a proper name ('son of Haggedolim').
notes.11:17: The Vulgate reads 'for praising and for giving thanks' (ad laudandum et ad confitendum), reflecting tehillah ('praise') where the Masoretic Text has techillah ('beginning').
notes.11:21: The Nethinim were a class of temple servants.
notes.11:25: Following the Clementine punctuation, 'and in the houses throughout all their regions' concludes the sentence from v. 24. Throughout vv. 25-31, 'daughters' (filiabus) preserves the literal Hebraism for dependent surrounding towns, and Cabseel (Kabzeel) corresponds to Hebrew Jekabzeel (cf. Josh 15:21).
notes.12:17: The Vulgate links Mijamin (Hebrew Miniamin) and Moadiah with et ('and') under a single leader, Piltai, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text leaves a gap after Miniamin; similarly, the Vulgate reads Shebaniah in v. 3 (Hebrew Shecaniah) and Adaiah in v. 16 (Hebrew Iddo).
notes.12:23: The Latin in libro verborum dierum ('in the book of the words of the days') renders the Hebrew idiom for 'chronicles' literally; the Vulgate also reads Jonathan here where the Hebrew has Johanan.
notes.12:33: Native Clementine Vulgate 12:33 combines Saints.Bible 12:33 and 12:34.
notes.12:38: The Vulgate reads turrim Emath ('the Tower of Emath') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the Tower of the Hundred (Hammeah), and portam gregis ('the Gate of the Flock') for the Sheep Gate.
notes.12:43: This verse preserves several distinctive Vulgate readings: principes civitatis ('leaders of the city') for Hebrew 'fields of the cities', in decore gratiarum actionis ('in the beauty of thanksgiving') for Hebrew 'portions of the law', and direct accusatives sacerdotes et Levitas ('the priests and the Levites') rather than 'for the priests and the Levites'.
notes.12:46: The Vulgate construes Levitas and filios Aaron as direct objects of sanctificabant ('consecrated the Levites ... consecrated the sons of Aaron'), whereas the Hebrew uses indirect objects ('set apart [holy portions] for the Levites ... for the sons of Aaron').
notes.13:5: The Vulgate reads 'for himself' (sibi) and 'before him' (ante eum), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'for him' (referring to Tobiah) and 'previously'.
notes.13:11: The Vulgate reads the first-person plural active 'Why have we forsaken' (Quare dereliquimus), including Nehemiah himself in the reproach, whereas the Hebrew reads passively 'Why is the house of God forsaken?'
notes.13:15: The Vulgate reads 'that they should sell on a day on which it was lawful to sell' (ut in die qua vendere liceret, venderent), whereas the Hebrew reads 'on the day they sold food'.
notes.13:19: The Vulgate reads 'when the gates of Jerusalem had grown quiet on the Sabbath day' (cum quievissent portæ Jerusalem in die sabbati), whereas the Hebrew refers to shadows falling on the gates before the Sabbath.
notes.13:27: The Vulgate reads 'Shall we also, being disobedient, do' (Numquid et nos inobedientes faciemus), whereas the Hebrew reads 'Shall we then listen to you to do'.
